why_ai: A risk-bearing balance sheet, licensed medical directors who alone may deny, and certifying actuaries protect the core, while claims, enrolment and review processing on screens is exposed.
why_clarity: Claims, authorizations and filings are well defined and recur by the million, but whether a medical-necessity or pricing judgement was right shows only through sparse appeals and next year's claims.
why_digital: Claims, records and models are digital work on screens; employers, seniors and states still buy through brokers, agents and contract procurements.

why_ai: Nurses and licensed medical directors make consequential, contested coverage decisions that regulators and state laws bar from full automation.
why_clarity: Criteria are written and requests recur in the tens of millions, but reviewers read the same packet differently and outcomes are rarely joined back.
why_digital: Requests and documents arrive electronically or by fax and are reviewed on screens; decisions go out as digital notices.

why_ai: Mostly approvable, criteria-matching requests are exactly what extraction models and auto-approval absorb; a licensed signer is needed only for denials.
why_clarity: Each request meets written criteria or not, at enormous volume, with approval rates and appeal outcomes as checkable feedback.
why_digital: Electronic submissions and attachments decided on screens, moving to a federal API.

why_ai: End-of-stay decisions are clinical, litigated and signed by licensed staff, with readmission and harm at stake.
why_clarity: Criteria guide length of stay, but trajectories vary by patient and the consequences of a cut-off show weeks later.
why_digital: Hospital and facility records reviewed remotely on screens; skilled nursing notes still arrive by fax.

why_ai: Certified coders validate diagnoses against records, a task NLP increasingly performs, though audit accountability keeps humans signing.
why_clarity: Coding rules and HCC models are codified and the work recurs per chart; RADV outcomes arrive years later.
why_digital: Retrieved records and submissions are entirely digital files worked on screens.

why_ai: Roster mapping, reconciliation and verification calls are mechanical work that models and voice agents absorb.
why_clarity: Each listing is right or wrong against what the office says, recurring across millions of records with secret-shopper checks.
why_digital: Spreadsheets, attestations and phone outreach feed a digital directory; groups deliver rosters on their own terms.

why_ai: Clock tracking, classification and case assembly automate; clinical reconsiderations need licensed reviewers.
why_clarity: Regulatory clocks, categories and file contents are codified, and audits test each case objectively.
why_digital: Requests arrive by phone, mail and fax and are worked as digital case files.

why_ai: Serving small plans means trusted outsourced capability under the same mandates, with judgement on thin data.
why_clarity: Deliverables such as ratings and risk scores are defined, but small denominators make results noisy and slow to read.
why_digital: Work is digital, though small plans buy through relationships and local health-system ties.

why_ai: Reaching and assessing frail, low-income members takes home visits, community workers and trust that software cannot supply.
why_clarity: Assessments and care plans follow a filed model of care, but whether coordination helped shows slowly.
why_digital: Members are reached by phone, mail and at the door; care plans live in software.

why_ai: Finding dated values in records against fixed specifications is extraction work models already do.
why_clarity: Each hit meets the specification or not, thousands of times a season, with an auditor's over-read as feedback.
why_digital: Retrieved records and abstraction are digital; retrieval depends on provider offices.

why_ai: Matching member-months across payer files and generating corrective transactions is deterministic automation; the plan's CMS attestations to enrolment and payment accuracy keep a named officer accountable for the result.
why_clarity: Expected versus received payment is an exact comparison repeated for every member every month.
why_digital: Electronic payer files in, electronic transactions out.

why_ai: Concept development takes clinical judgement, but claim scanning and coding review are what models absorb.
why_clarity: Findings are checkable against policy and contract, recur at scale, and are tested in provider disputes.
why_digital: Claims data in, findings and recoveries out, sold to plans remotely.

why_ai: Tracking launches, exclusivity dates and litigation from public sources is work language models increasingly do, though trusted analysts' calls on patent outcomes keep subscriptions; scored like the pharma-facing pipeline twin.
why_clarity: Drug and exclusivity records repeat across thousands of products, and each dated call is checked against the later approval, launch or generic entry.
why_digital: Public filings and dockets in, subscription research out, entirely online.

why_ai: Clients pay for trusted experts' reading of novel rules and politics, which AI assists but does not replace.
why_clarity: Impact estimates are defined, but much work is bespoke and policy outcomes resolve slowly.
why_digital: Public files and models in, reports out, sold through relationships in Washington.

why_ai: Credentialed actuaries must certify bids and rate filings personally and carry the professional liability.
why_clarity: Actuarial standards and templates codify the work, which recurs annually, but pricing is judged a year or more later.
why_digital: Client data and models in, filings out, all digital and remote.

why_ai: Actuaries stand behind the estimates and the pooled dataset is hard to replicate, though computation does most of the work.
why_clarity: Transfer estimates recur five times a year on a fixed method and are graded by HHS each June.
why_digital: Issuer data files in, Excel reports out, entirely remote.

why_ai: Rates must be certified by credentialed actuaries and defended to CMS and plans.
why_clarity: Rate development follows federal rules and recurs annually, but adequacy shows in plans' results later.
why_digital: State data in, certifications out; won through state procurements.

why_ai: Federal mandate and independence protect the function; validation tasks automate.
why_clarity: Protocols define each activity and recur per plan per year, with a statutory report date.
why_digital: Plan data and records reviewed remotely, with some on-site work; reports published online.

why_ai: Survey design and syndicated reporting are increasingly automatable, though brand trust matters.
why_clarity: Studies repeat annually on stable instruments, but what predicts member choice is debated.
why_digital: Online and phone surveys in, digital reports out.

why_ai: Chart reading for diagnoses is the extraction task NLP coding is replacing; coders remain for validation.
why_clarity: Coding guidelines are codified and charts recur by the million, with audit outcomes as feedback.
why_digital: Records retrieved and coded digitally, delivered as files.

why_ai: Cut-point forecasting is model work; trusted advice on strategy carries some durability.
why_clarity: Forecasts are graded every October against published cut points.
why_digital: Public CMS data in, forecasts and advice out, remotely.

why_ai: Appointed and certifying actuaries sign, and trend judgement is consequential with slow feedback.
why_clarity: Bids and filings are defined and recur, but pricing accuracy shows a year or more later.
why_digital: Internal claims data and models on screens; outputs filed with regulators.

why_ai: A standard-setter whose measures regulators adopt has institutional permanence.
why_clarity: Specifications and accreditation standards are codified and updated annually.
why_digital: Plan submissions and standards handled digitally; accreditation includes reviews.

why_ai: Protocol-bound survey fielding is commodity work; CMS approval gives some durability.
why_clarity: CMS protocols fix every step, repeated each year per contract.
why_digital: Mail and phone responses in, files submitted to CMS.

why_ai: Compiling public filings into databases is the work AI-native data tools do directly.
why_clarity: Filings are structured and recur quarterly, and the data reconciles to source.
why_digital: Public files in, subscription databases out.

why_ai: A trusted neutral steward of contributed claims is hard to replace; analysis itself automates.
why_clarity: Research questions vary and findings are judged by peers over time.
why_digital: De-identified claims in an enclave, reports and licences out.

why_ai: Statutory authority and accountable regulators keep the function, though review tasks automate.
why_clarity: Review standards are written and filings recur annually, but rate adequacy shows later.
why_digital: Filings handled electronically; jurisdiction is local by statute.

why_ai: Delivering primary care under risk is in-person clinical work by licensed clinicians patients trust.
why_clarity: Cost and quality targets are defined, but which care decisions produced them shows slowly.
why_digital: Care is delivered in clinics and homes; analytics run on screens.

why_ai: Statutory commissions advising Congress on novel policy questions have permanent mandates.
why_clarity: Reports follow statutory dates, but the questions change and policy effects show years later.
why_digital: Federal data in, public reports out, to a single statutory audience.

why_ai: Licensed physicians must decide external reviews personally under statute.
why_clarity: Each case is decided against criteria under a clock, recurring at volume.
why_digital: Case files reviewed remotely, determinations delivered electronically.

why_ai: Advocacy relationships carry the value, while briefs and comment drafting automate.
why_clarity: Success in advocacy is contested and slow to judge.
why_digital: Policy work is digital, but influence is exercised in person.
